en.title: FAZ covers partial collapse of Putin's bridge, Nvidia chip restrictions, and Orbán party crisis
en.dek: FAZ reports partial collapse of Kerch Bridge after drone attacks, Nvidia chip restrictions amid China smuggling, and Orbán party crisis.
facts: Kerch Bridge partially collapsed after Ukrainian drone attacks in November 2026, with the main span falling into water.
Russian-installed Crimean governor Sergei Aksyonov initially denied the destruction, citing unfavorable regime news.
Nvidia chips were officially banned from China but reportedly entered via smuggling routes, according to FAZ.
Orbán's party faces internal crisis, though specific details are not provided in the sources.
body:
The Kerch Bridge, spanning the Strait of Kerch, was partially destroyed after Ukrainian drone attacks overnight into Tuesday, November 17, 2026. The main white arch collapsed into the water, while road ends remained, and the nearby railway bridge appeared intact. Russian-installed Crimean Governor Sergei Aksyonov did not initially confirm the collapse, a pattern when news is unfavorable for the Putin regime, though Moscow later announced a commission to address reconstruction and traffic organization. Traffic had been halted after the drone attacks on Monday, partially resumed with restrictions, and then struck again when the main arch collapsed at a 15-degree tilt, which pro-Kremlin Telegram channel Mash estimated. Putin's spokesman called the damage "insignificant."

China officially banned Nvidia chips from entering the country, but they arrived via smuggling routes, FAZ reported. The report questions how far China has progressed in its chip catch-up effort despite these restrictions. Putin's spokesman called the damage "insignificant."

Orbán's party faces an internal crisis, though the sources do not detail the specific nature of the dispute.

The Kerch Bridge is a key supply route for both military and civilian needs on the annexed Crimea, which Russia took in 2014. Ukrainian forces have increasingly targeted the bridge with drones this year, making supply lines more difficult. The bridge holds symbolic importance for Putin, who described it in 2016 as a project linking historical Russian ambitions with the new Crimea, and later called it a "Symbol of the Reunification" of Crimea with Russia. The bridge was built by Arkady Rotenberg, a childhood friend of Putin, for over three billion euros and opened in 2018.

China's official ban on Nvidia chips has not stopped their flow into the country, as smuggling routes have become the alternative delivery method. The FAZ report notes the gap between the official restriction and the reality on the ground, though it does not assess the technical success of China's chip development program. The report does not specify when the smuggling routes were established or the volume of chips moving through them.

Orbán's party crisis reflects internal tensions within the Hungarian ruling party, though the sources provided do not elaborate on the causes or key figures involved in the dispute.
en.context: The Kerch Bridge connects Russian mainland to Crimea, a territory Russia annexed from Ukraine in 2014. Ukraine has targeted the bridge with drones to disrupt supply lines. Nvidia chips are advanced semiconductors subject to export controls, with China seeking to develop domestic alternatives despite bans. Orbán leads the Fidesz party in Hungary, which has faced internal criticism.
